# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally

# Intake Brief: RCA — audit Phase 1 / Phase 2 Reliability

**Work Item:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL

## Headline Summary

Conduct a root cause analysis of why the audit pipeline (Phase 1 screening and Phase 2 deep analysis) frequently fails or degrades, quantify the failure modes from debug logs and stored audit reports, and produce a prioritised set of reliability recommendations with follow-up work items.

## Problem Statement

Audits routinely report `Ready to close: No` for *infrastructure* reasons rather than genuine code defects — concurrency saturation aborting Phase 1 parent screens, wall-clock budget exhaustion silently skipping children, a misleading `parse_failure` debug label that fires on successful calls, and in-main-slot child screens left pending. This forces manual re-audits and blocks releases. No single RCA quantifies these modes or ranks fixes.

## Users

- **Release operator** running an automated audit: needs reliable verdicts without manual re-audits.
- **Producer** reviewing audit results: needs trustworthy signals to make release decisions.
- **Agent** running audits: needs predictable behaviour and actionable failure diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A written RCA quantifies failure modes from at least 30 days of evidence, grouped by phase (Phase 1 parent, Phase 1 child, Phase 2 parent deep, Phase 2 child deep, false-positive screen) and by root cause, with reproducible commands/queries and representative examples.
2. The RCA explicitly confirms or refutes **F1** (the `parse_failure` label fires on successful calls) and states the effect on observability; it must distinguish label noise from genuine parse failures.
3. Every failure mode in the RCA is backed by a count and at least one concrete example (item id + log path or report excerpt).
4. A prioritised recommendation list is produced (impact × effort), each item naming the concrete change, the expected reliability effect, and the observable signal that would confirm improvement.
5. Recommendations cover, at minimum: JSON-output contract robustness (e.g. JSON-first prompting / schema retry / fenced-block tolerant parsing), timeout and wall-clock budget right-sizing, concurrency saturation and queue-wait policy, child-audit execution strategy (in-main-slot vs separate-process), provider-error retry policy, and debug-log observability (a correct, non-misleading reason taxonomy).
6. Each accepted recommendation is captured as a follow-up work item (child of this item or `discovered-from`) with its own testable ACs; rejected recommendations record the rationale.
7. UK English throughout; no code changes are required by this item other than producing the RCA/recommendations (implementation lands via the follow-ups).

## Constraints

- Read-only analysis of logs and stored reports; do not modify the audit runner as part of this item.
- Use bounded reads for large log stores (stream, filter by context/reason); never unbounded recursive grep over `.worklog/`.
- Do not close or reopen unrelated work items; link to the prior art below instead.

## Evidence Sources

1. **Debug corpus:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` (91 files analysed; raw Pi streams + the logged `reason` field).
2. **Stored audit reports:** `wl show` worklog data (rawOutput per item; counts from 2026-09-15 export).
3. **Runner source:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_call_pi`, `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, `_extract_json_array`, Phase 1/Phase 2 call sites).
4. **Log files:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` (audit runs with verdicts and diagnostics).

## Preliminary Findings (to be verified and extended)

### F1 — The debug-log `reason: parse_failure` label is misleading (observability bug)

**Confirmed.** Code inspection of `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` (L4828) shows:

```python
elif isinstance(result, dict) and (result.get("raw_stdout") or result.get("raw_stderr")):
    reason = "provider_error" if result.get("_provider_error") else "parse_failure"
```

The label fires whenever `raw_stdout` or `raw_stderr` is present — which is true on **every** successful call. Corpus analysis of 91 JSONL debug files shows:

- 91 files, all containing `parse_failure` entries as the dominant reason.
- Only 5 files contain `provider_error` (total: ~10 provider_error entries across the corpus).
- Only 2 files contain `debug_log` entries (explicit debug log path was provided).

The preliminary finding of ~92–95% false-positive rate is confirmed — the `parse_failure` label is an observability bug that invalidates any failure analysis keyed on it.

### F2 — Genuine JSON-contract failures are real but rare (~5–8%)

**To be verified.** The preliminary finding cites 34 genuine failures in 285 real-project logs. This count requires verification against the actual debug corpus — checking which `parse_failure` entries actually contain unparseable content vs. parseable content mislabelled by the F1 bug.

### F3 — Wall-clock budget exhaustion dominates (child skips + Phase 2 timeouts)

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple log entries show:
- "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — Phase 2 skipped after Phase 1 detected blocking issues.
- Parent-process timeout budgets vary widely (~120s, 900s, 1500s, 3110s) — inconsistent right-sizing.
- Stored report data (from prior audit): `Skipped due to audit timeout` ~176, `Audit runner skipped this child after Ns` ~100+.

### F4 — Concurrency saturation aborts Phase 1

**Confirmed.** Log files show repeated "Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated: no slot within 90s" and "Audit concurrency limit reached: semaphore 'audit' busy: no slot free within 0.0s (max_workers=1)". Phase 1 parent screens return `unmet` with zero Pi calls made.

### F5 — In-main-slot child screens leave children unverified

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple entries show "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — child ACs left in `partial (pending main-session review)` state when the main session does not run the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` prompts.

### F6 — Provider errors

**Confirmed.** Corpus analysis: ~10 `provider_error` entries across 91 files (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ: 3, SA-0MSM6VU2K001IMVP: 1, SA-0MSUT8GQP004WSYN: 1, SA-0MSNYMKV7005P0H9: 1, SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42: 1). Provider errors are currently conflated with the misleading `parse_failure` label.

## Recommendations (Preliminary — to be finalised)

| Rec | Priority | Impact | Effort | Description | Follow-up Work Item |
|-----|----------|--------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| R1 | High | High | Low | Fix the debug-log reason taxonomy (observability) | SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99 (R1) |
| R2 | High | High | Medium | Harden JSON contract (JSON-first + tolerant + re-ask) | SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I (R2) |
| R3 | High | High | Medium | Right-size wall-clock budgets; stop silent child skips | SA-0MU32T6O0001UALR (R3) — in_review |
| R4 | High | High | Low-Medium | Priority queue for Phase 1 parent screen | SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ (R4) — in_review |
| R5 | Medium-High | High | Low | Enforce child-audit execution contract | SA-0MU32TE120012T49 (R5) |
| R6 | Medium | Medium | Low | Separate provider errors from parse failures | SA-0MU32TFKB0012ALC (R6) — blocked on R1 |
| R7 | Medium | Medium | Low | Emit per-run reliability summary | SA-0MU32TH89000YHP9 (R7) — blocked on R1, R6 |

## Related Work (Prior Art — all evaluated)

| Work Item | Title | Status | Relevance |
|-----------|-------|--------|-----------|
| SA-0MPOGKY8U007K206 | Add debug logging for Pi responses | completed | Introduced current reason label (root of F1) |
| SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8 | Parse JSON array from mixed analysis+JSON | completed | Prior art for JSON contract (R2) |
| SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A | Audit runner bugs | completed | Prior art for JSON parse fallback |
| SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC | Consolidate duplicate Pi JSON parsers | **open, plan_complete** | Should be consulted before R2 implementation |
| SA-0MSF4AFXF000M5DN | Right-size parent-timeout guard | completed | Prior art for budget right-sizing (R3) |
| SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X | Configurable cumulative elapsed-time guard | completed | Prior art for timeout guards |
| SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL | Fail immediately on concurrency limit | completed | Prior art superseded by queue admission |
| SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9 | Phase 2 deep-analysis timeout | completed | Prior art for timeout issues |
| SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE | In-main-slot child audit mode | — | Prior art for R5 |
| SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 | Motivating audit (2026-09-15) | — | Source of this RCA |

## Existing State

The audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) has 10+ call sites for `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`. The debug-log reason taxonomy is set in a single branch (L4906) but is overly broad. The `_extract_json_array` parser exists but does not handle fenced blocks or prose-prefixed JSON consistently. Concurrency is managed via a priority queue with `max_workers=2` (configurable). Wall-clock budgets are set ad-hoc across multiple call sites.

## Desired Change

A comprehensive RCA documenting all failure modes with quantified counts, examples, and reproducible queries — followed by a prioritised recommendation list that feeds into the already-created follow-up work items (R1–R7).

## Key Files (predicted for RCA analysis)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — All call sites, timeout guards, concurrency, parse logic
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` — 91 debug log files (reason taxonomy analysis)
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` — 100+ audit run log files (verdict/diagnostic analysis)
- `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — Stored audit reports (rawOutput per item)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The 91 debug JSONL files and 100+ log files are representative of the 30-day evidence window required by AC1.
- **Assumption:** The preliminary counts (F1–F6) from the 2026-09-15 audit export are approximately correct and need refinement, not re-invention.
- **Risk:** The debug corpus may be incomplete — some audits may not have written debug files (e.g., early failures before debug logging was enabled).
- **Risk:** The existing child work items (R1–R7) may need revision based on findings — e.g., if R3 is confirmed as the dominant failure mode, its priority should be elevated.
- **Scope creep:** This is a read-only analysis item. Implementation work should only happen in the follow-up child work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the debug corpus cover the required 30-day evidence window? — A: The 91 JSONL files span from 2026-08-12 to 2026-09-15 (~34 days), meeting the requirement.
- Q: Should the RCA include analysis of non-SorraAgents projects? — A: The RCA focuses on SorraAgents debug logs; other projects' debug logs can be consulted if patterns differ significantly.

- **SA-0MSRMFSZL007CZVQ** – Documentation — update scope semantics (completed)

# R1 — Audit debug log mislabels every successful call as `parse_failure`

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi_and_maybe_log` sets
`reason = "parse_failure"` whenever the Pi result carries `raw_stdout`/`raw_stderr`.
But `raw_stdout` is present on **every successful call**, so the debug log
labels successful calls as parse failures.

Evidence (2026-09-15 corpus scan):

- 19,663 `~/.audit_debug/**/audit_debug_*.jsonl` files; 39,619 entries with
  `reason: parse_failure` vs only 26 with `provider_error`.
- Re-running `extract_pi_text()` + `_extract_json_array()` over real-project
  logs (285 files) shows ~92-95% of `parse_failure` entries parse cleanly:
  `parent` 158/172, `phase2_deep` 93/98, `false-positive-screen` 41/43.
- Genuine parse failures in real-project logs: ~34.

Consequence: any failure analysis keyed on this label is invalid, and the
false funnel made the reliability RCA (SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL) far harder.

## Desired change

Replace the blanket label with an accurate taxonomy: a neutral default reason
(e.g. `call_trace`) for calls that returned, plus an explicit parse-outcome
flag set by the call site, and `parse_failure` only when the expected JSON
shape genuinely could not be extracted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` no longer records `reason: parse_failure` for a
   call whose output was successfully parsed at the call site.
2. The debug entry carries an explicit parse-outcome field (e.g. `parse_ok:
   true|false`) and a neutral reason for successful calls.
3. A genuine parse failure is still recorded distinctly (labelled
   `parse_failure` or equivalent) and is machine-distinguishable from a
   successful call.
4. Provider errors remain labelled `provider_error` and are not conflated with
   parse failures.
5. Unit tests cover: successful call -> not `parse_failure`; genuine parse
   failure -> labelled; provider error -> `provider_error`.
6. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the reason taxonomy; existing
   debug-log tests/consumers are updated.
7. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not change audit verdict semantics; this is observability only.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, call sites.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — debug-log taxonomy.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — debug-log tests.

## Evidence trail

- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0.jsonl` (labelled
  `parse_failure`, yet the screen produced valid classifications).
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MTCSPA5H007IQ59.jsonl` (parent).

## Summary
Derive right-sized parent-process and per-call budgets from measured per-call timing (p50/p95 per phase).

# Resume completion for budget-exceeded children

# Intake: Audit-runner pi calls crash with `Connection error.` from stale-ctx extension exceptions

## Problem statement

Audit-runner `pi` subprocesses crash mid-call and the runner records
`provider_error: Connection error.` because pi extensions loaded into the audit
session throw on a **stale `ExtensionContext`** after pi replaces or reloads the
session. The **fatal uncaught exception** is thrown by the ContextHub-owned
`worklog` recovery extension (`register-recovery.ts`, `_notifyFn` →
`ctx.ui.notify`), not by `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. Two
SorraAgents-owned extensions (`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals`)
throw the *same* stale-ctx error but pi catches those and prints them as
(non-fatal) `Extension error (...)` lines. This blocks audits and therefore the
ship final-validation gate (exit 12).

## Users

- **Release manager** — needs audits to complete so `dev` → `main` is not blocked
  by spurious provider failures.
  - *As a release manager, I want an audit pi call to return a genuine verdict
    even after an extension-triggered session replacement, so the release gate
    is not blocked by an infrastructure crash.*
- **Audit operator** — needs `provider_error` entries in the debug corpus to
  reflect real provider faults, not extension crashes.
  - *As an audit operator, I want the audit debug log to distinguish a real
    provider fault from an extension exception, so I can triage correctly.*
- **Pi extension maintainer** — needs extensions to fail safe when the session
  they were registered against is replaced.
  - *As a maintainer, I want my extension's async callbacks to no-op when the
    captured ctx is invalid, so a session swap cannot crash an unrelated run.*

## Existing state (evidence)

The failure was captured for the audit of **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** (now deleted).
The debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
(`context=parent`) records:

- `reason: provider_error`, `provider_error: "Connection error."`,
  `elapsed_seconds: ~713`.
- `raw_stderr` contains one `Extension error
  (/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts): This
  extension ctx is stale ...` line, one identical line for
  `proxy-sse-signals`, and then the **fatal, uncaught** trace:

  ```
  Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. ...
      at ExtensionRunner.assertActive (...)
      at get ui (...)
      at _notifyFn (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts:71:41)
      at _notifyRetryAttempt (.../register-recovery.ts:549:5)
      at triggerInvisibleContinue (.../register-recovery.ts:391:7)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (...)
  Node.js v22.22.1
  ```

  The trailing `Node.js v22.22.1` banner shows the pi process **crashed**; the
  audit runner then surfaced `Connection error.` from the pi JSON stream.

Corpus scan across every `reason=provider_error` entry
(`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl`) shows **all** non-empty
`raw_stderr` provider errors carry the `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx stack;
some also carry the `proxy-compaction-bridge` / `proxy-sse-signals`
`Extension error` lines (non-fatal, caught by pi).

Root cause of each stale access:

- `ContextHub .../register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` is assigned a closure over
  the *handler's* `ctx` (`_notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(...)`,
  lines ~84/87/212) and is later invoked from the async retry loop
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`). If the session was replaced/reloaded in
  between, `ctx.ui` throws — and because the call originates in a timer/async
  callback, pi never catches it and the process dies.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — both `after_provider_response`
  and `context` handlers call `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` on the event
  ctx; a stale ctx throws.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — `turn_start` captures `ctx.ui` as
  `statusUi`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls `statusUi.setStatus(...)`
  on the stale UI handle.

`pi` supports `--no-extensions` / `-ne` (disables extension discovery), alongside
the `--no-context-files --no-skills` flags the audit runner already adds to
`_call_pi`. Audit prompts are read-only and fully self-contained, so they do not
depend on extensions.

## Desired change

1. **Unblock audit calls (SorraAgents-owned):** stop loading interactive/UI
   extensions in audit-runner pi subprocesses — add `--no-extensions` to the
   `_call_pi` command (mirroring the existing context-reduction flags).
2. **Harden the SorraAgents-owned extensions:** make `proxy-compaction-bridge`
   and `proxy-sse-signals` fail safe on a stale/replaced ctx — never call
   `ctx.ui`/`ctx.sessionManager` on an invalidated ctx (guard, re-capture from a
   fresh handler, or no-op/passthrough).
3. **Fatal crash (cross-repo handoff — delivered):** the ContextHub
   `worklog` recovery-extension stale-ctx crash is handed off to
   **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (`Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale
   ExtensionContext after session replacement (_notifyFn)`), which is not edited
   from this SorraAgents work item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No extension crash on audit calls:** the audit runner's `_call_pi` command
   excludes extension discovery (`--no-extensions`). Verified by a unit test
   asserting the constructed command (both tool-enabled and tool-disabled paths).
2. **Stale-ctx-safe SorraAgents extensions:** `proxy-compaction-bridge` and
   `proxy-sse-signals` no-op (context passthrough / status unchanged) when their
   handler or async callback observes an invalidated `ctx`, never throwing.
   Verified by `node:test` unit tests injecting a stale-ctx stub.
3. **Re-audit completes genuinely:** a re-audit of SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB (or an
   equivalent audit pi call that triggers a session replacement) completes with a
   genuine verdict (`met`/`partial`/`adjusted`) and the debug entry's `reason` is
   not `provider_error` with `Connection error.` attributable to an extension
   exception.
4. **Regression tests:** a stale/replaced-session-ctx regression test exists for
   both `pi-client` extensions (Node unit tests) and a Python test asserts the
   audit `_call_pi` command includes `--no-extensions`; the tests fail against
   the pre-fix code.
5. **Docs + full suite:** `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` (F6) are updated to reflect the corrected
   attribution/fix; all related documentation (code comments, README, docs) is
   updated; and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo boundary:** the fatal crash is in
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` (separate repo and `WL-` worklog). It is
  **not** edited from this item; the fix is tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B.
- **Do not regress** the compaction-bridge wire contract
  (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) or the dispatch reshape semantics/tests.
- **Do not weaken fail-closed audit behaviour**; the audit runner must still
  return `unmet`/`partial` on genuine provider errors, not mask them.
- `--no-extensions` affects all discovered extensions in audit calls only; the
  interactive TUI extension behaviour (compaction mirroring, status line,
  recovery) must remain unchanged.
- `wl`-tracked, test-first, build → test → commit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi` builds the pi command
  (~L3648); add `--no-extensions`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — command-flag tests (~L267–304);
  add the `--no-extensions` assertion.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — guard/re-bind the session id
  used by `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js` — pure core (no ctx
  access); keep behaviour, extend tests only.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — guard the captured `statusUi` used by
  the capturing-fetch callback.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
  `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` — stale-ctx regression coverage.
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`, `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` —
  documentation/correction.
- *(cross-repo, tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B)*
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`.

## Related work (manual)

- **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** — `[test-failure] getCompletedOrInReviewItems ...`
  (`discovered-from`; the audit that failed with this signature; now deleted).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for
  child audits in the final-validation gate (records the same failure as the
  motivation for removing manual interruptions).
- **SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL** — RCA: Audit Pipeline Reliability
  (`docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`); F6 documents the 9 `provider_error`
  entries (incl. `Connection error.`) and their conflation with parse failures.
- **SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0** — origin of `proxy-compaction-bridge` (wire contract
  LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- **SA-0MSHAKSEA001LQ6T** — origin of `proxy-sse-signals`.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — audit context reduction
  (`--no-context-files --no-skills`); precedent for adding a loader flag to
  `_call_pi`.
- **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (ContextHub) — handoff item for the fatal
  `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/cross-repo).** Debug-log evidence shows the *fatal* uncaught
  exception is thrown by the ContextHub-owned `worklog` extension
  (`register-recovery.ts`), not `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. How should
  this item be scoped?
  - Answer (producer): **(c) analysis/handoff** — do not edit ContextHub from this
    item; **create a `WL-` item** for the fatal `register-recovery` crash, and do
    the SorraAgents-side extensions/audit fixes + tests here.
  - Evidence: created **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** in ContextHub; SorraAgents-side
    work captured in the ACs above (consistent with Q3 = (a), which names tests
    for the `pi-client` extensions and the audit `--no-extensions` command).
- **Q2 (audit extension policy).** Is disabling extension discovery for
  audit-runner pi calls (`pi ... --no-extensions`, alongside
  `--no-context-files --no-skills`) acceptable?
  - Answer (producer): **n/a** — not separately decided; Q3(a) explicitly names
    the `--no-extensions` command assertion, so it is in scope (AC1/AC4).
- **Q3 (regression-test surface).** Where should the stale-ctx regression test
  live?
  - Answer (producer): **(a)** Node unit tests for both `pi-client` extensions
    plus a Python test asserting the audit pi command includes `--no-extensions`.
  - Recorded as AC4.

## Problem statement

The Discord ship report embed title is hardcoded as `Release vX.Y.Z` and does not include the project name from the worklog config. Additionally, the report description should include the project name for clarity.

## Users

- **Release operator**: Wants the Discord notification to clearly identify which project is being released, especially when monitoring multiple project releases.

1. The Discord embed title changes from `Release vX.Y.Z` to `<ProjectName> Release vX.Y.Z`, where `<ProjectName>` is read from the worklog config's `projectName` field.

4. The embed description includes the project name alongside the version for added clarity.

## Constraints

- Non-breaking change — existing webhook behaviour must not be affected.

## Existing state

- The `parseSimpleYaml()` function already parses `projectName` from config (verified in tests).
- `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` already follows the correct precedence pattern.
- The `sendReleaseNotification()` function resolves the webhook URL but does not read `projectName`.

## Desired change

1. Add a `resolveProjectName(projectRoot)` helper (parallel to `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl`) that reads `projectName` from the worklog config.
2. Update `sendReleaseNotification()` to resolve the project name and pass it to `buildDiscordPayload()`.
3. Update `buildDiscordPayload()` to accept a `projectName` parameter and include it in the embed title and description.

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out (many concurrent `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes) ran the test suite with a **leaked `GIT_DIR`** pointing at a live worktree's git dir. Tests that use real `git` (git init/commit/push fixtures) therefore operated on the **live repository** instead of their temp dirs: they committed 24 junk commits (`init`/`Initial commit`, authors `Test <test@test.com>`, `T <t@t>`, `Cache Test`, `RT Test`) on top of the then-current `dev` tip and **pushed them to `origin/dev`**, gutting the branch (483 files, -144,702 lines).

This is the exact incident class documented in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (2026-09-24 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 / docs/dev/test-isolation.md) — the sandbox helper neutralises the vars for test fixtures, but the **production test-execution path does not**.

## Evidence

- Orphaned (`PPID 1`) `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes with env:
  `GIT_DIR=/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.git/worktrees/wl-OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT-nested-node-modules`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core`, `GIT_PREFIX=`.
- Their `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` children inherited the same `GIT_DIR`.
- `refs/heads/dev` reflog: last legitimate entry `763b8f11` (push by Sorra the Orc), then 24 test commits by `T/Test/Cache Test/RT Test`.
- `refs/heads/dev` and the shared `.git/config` (`core.bare=true`) were rewritten; `.git/HEAD` moved to junk.
- `git ls-remote origin dev` showed the junk tip `6366f913` (fast-forward from `763b8f11`, so the push was accepted).

## Impact

- `origin/dev` overwritten (recovered to `763b8f11` via `--force-with-lease` by the implement session).
- Shared main checkout `core.bare=true`, `dev` ref clobbered (recovered).
- Collateral: another agent's uncommitted work in the main checkout was reset/lost.
- Any push/CI consuming `dev` during the window would have seen the gutted tree.

## Root cause / propagation

- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner` does `env = os.environ.copy()` and passes it to `subprocess.run` **without stripping `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`**. `GIT_DIR` overrides `cwd` for every git subprocess, so fixture `git init/commit/push` hit the live repo.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_run_tests_via_test_skill` -> `run_cached`) have the same gap.
- The origin of the leaked `GIT_DIR` in the launcher is external to `skill/` (no setter found in the repo); the audit fan-out was orphaned. **Defence-in-depth must not depend on the launcher being clean.**

## Proposed fix

1. Scrub `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` (from `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) in `test_cache._default_runner` (and any other subprocess that runs tests) before spawning — single choke point.
2. `run_tests.py`: strip the same vars in its runner/env.
3. `audit_runner.py`: strip before `run_cached`/`run_tests`; ensure per-item audits cannot fan out unbounded (34+ concurrent observed).
4. Regression test: with `GIT_DIR` set to the live repo in `os.environ`, a fixture `git init/commit` must NOT touch  the live checkout (extend `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`).
5. Consider making the live-repo guard fail-fast (abort the run) rather than only post-hoc, and have `run_tests.py` refuse to run when `GIT_DIR`/override vars are present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_cache._default_runner` (and `run_tests.py`/`audit_runner.py`) remove `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` before spawning tests.
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the leak (fixture mutation under a poisoned `GIT_DIR`) and proves the scrub prevents it.
- [ ] `origin/dev` cannot be moved by any test fixture (asserted).
- [ ] Audit fan-out is bounded (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` honoured; no 30+ concurrent orphans).
- [ ] Full suite green.

# live-repo mutation guard false-positives when the suite runs inside an agent worktree

`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`

## Problem statement

When the full test suite runs **inside an agent worktree** (the normal `implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` case), the live-repo mutation guard anchors its agent-worktree exclusion on the *passed root* rather than the **main checkout**. Inside a linked worktree that root is the worktree itself, so `excluded_refs` is always empty and any concurrent agent committing to another worktree is reported as a mutation — failing the run and blocking the full-suite release gate for every agent whenever the shared host has more than one active session.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `/skill:test` or `implement.py finish` from inside an `implement` worktree on a shared multi-agent host.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the full-suite exit code as the pre-push release gate.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of the shared `git_sandbox.py` helper and the two guards that consume it.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the full suite to run green inside my worktree even while sibling agents commit to theirs, so that concurrent sessions do not block my release gate.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout, so that real corruption (the `GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want one shared fix in `git_sandbox.py`, so the outer `run_tests.py` guard and the inner `live_repo_guard.py` conftest guard cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `snapshot_repo_state()` called with a **linked-worktree root** returns `excluded_refs` containing every branch checked out in a registered worktree under the **main checkout's** `.worklog/worktrees/` (not `<passed_root>/.worklog/worktrees`). Verification: a unit test creates a main repo plus an agent worktree, calls `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)`, and asserts the agent worktree's `refs/heads/wl-*` is in `excluded_refs`.
- [ ] **No false positive:** with the guard/snapshot armed at a linked-worktree root, advancing a branch checked out in a *sibling* agent worktree produces `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] == False` and does not fail the guard. Verification: a nested-pytest test that arms the guard inside a worktree, commits in a sibling worktree, and asserts exit code 0 with no `live-repo mutation` text (red on the pre-fix helper).
- [ ] **No false negative:** an in-place mutation of the guarded checkout is still reported — (a) moving `HEAD`/the guarded branch ref, (b) modifying a tracked file, (c) adding an untracked non-ignored file. Verification: the existing `TestSnapshotContract` cases still pass when the guard is armed at a worktree root.
- [ ] **Worktree registration churn does not fail:** registering or removing a worktree under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` during a guarded run does not fail the guard when the reportable diff is empty. Verification: a unit test where `excluded_refs` grows but `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False` asserts the per-test guard does not fail.
- [ ] **Single shared fix:** both the `run_tests.py` outer guard (`_detect_live_repo_mutation`) and the conftest inner guard (`live_repo_guard.py`) exhibit the corrected behaviour, with the anchoring logic living only in `git_sandbox.py`. Verification: code review plus the guard-level nested-pytest tests.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the reported failure (red against the pre-fix helper) and passes after the fix, covering the `wl-SA-0MUD5R5EQ...-fix-inherited-pass...` worktree scenario and the observed `moved ref refs/heads/wl-*` suite failures.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. This includes the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring's exclusion-derivation note and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` must remain **stdlib-only** and loadable by file location — the repo-root `conftest.py` loads it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and must not mutate `sys.path`.
- Agent-worktree exclusion must be **derived from git plumbing** (e.g. `git worktree list --porcelain`, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to locate the main checkout) — **never** a `wl-*` name pattern. The module docstring documents why: a name pattern would also exclude the incident's own fixture branches and destroy detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX class of bug.
- Snapshots stay **read-only**: only plumbing commands; never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch`, or `--refresh`.
- The fix must not weaken genuine mutation detection (moved `dev`, config rewrites, tracked/untracked file changes).
- Any extra git invocation per snapshot must be cheap and confined to the snapshot path; it must not turn the per-test fingerprint into a full `status` scan.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` computes `agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`, where `root` is the passed root (for `snapshot_repo_state`, the `git_toplevel(resolved)` of the passed path).
- Reproduced 2026-09-26 on `dev @ 10995367`:
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from the **main checkout** → `excluded_refs` contains all 12 agent-worktree branches.
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` → `git_toplevel` is the worktree root and `excluded_refs == set()`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` arms with `root` from `_default_root(config)` (or the repo-root conftest's `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent`, which inside a worktree is the worktree root).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` where `project_root` comes from `detect_project_root()` (worktree root when run inside one). It shares the same helper and the same defect.
- Adjacent defect (same guard path, reproduced): `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))`, and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails whenever the fingerprint differs — regardless of `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]`. Adding a second worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/` mid-run changes `excluded` while the diff stays clean, so worktree registration churn is a second false positive.
- Existing tests only arm the guard at the **main** root (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestLiveRepoGuard::test_agent_worktree_churn_does_not_trip_the_guard` creates the worktree under the root it arms), so they do not exercise the linked-worktree case.

Minimal reproduction (from any linked worktree):

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents")
from skill.shared import git_sandbox as gs
snap = gs.snapshot_repo_state(".")
print(snap["root"], len(snap["worktrees"]), snap["excluded_refs"])
PY
# from a worktree: excluded_refs == set()  (bug)
# from the main checkout: excluded_refs has every agent-worktree branch
```

## Desired change

- Add a small helper that resolves the **main checkout root** from git plumbing (first entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`, or the parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), and anchor agent-worktree exclusion on `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` rather than the passed root.
- Thread that anchor through `_parse_worktrees` / `snapshot_repo_state`. When the passed root *is* the main checkout the behaviour is unchanged; when it is a linked worktree the exclusion set is now populated correctly.
- Make the per-test guard fail only when `diff_snapshots` reports a reportable change (or exclude the `excluded`-set churn from the fingerprint), so worktree registration/deregistration is not a false positive while the authoritative full diff still catches real mutations.
- Add regression tests at both levels (helper and guard) and document the main-checkout anchoring in the module docstring and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Add a main-checkout resolver and change `_parse_worktrees`/`snapshot_repo_state` to anchor `agent_root` on `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/`; address `fingerprint()`/`diff_snapshots` treatment of the excluded set. Module docstring's exclusion-derivation note needs updating.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `pytest_runtest_teardown` must fail only when the authoritative diff is non-empty (not merely when the cheap fingerprint moves); affects `__init__`, `pytest_runtest_teardown`, `pytest_sessionfinish`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — Add `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)` exclusion test, sibling-churn no-false-positive test, in-place mutation still-reported test, and excluded-set-churn test (class `TestAgentWorktreeExclusion`).
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Add a nested-pytest test that arms the guard from inside a linked worktree and commits in a sibling worktree (exit 0, no `live-repo mutation` text); keep the existing main-root test.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Verify `_detect_live_repo_mutation` benefits from the shared fix; add a focused test if the outer guard needs its own coverage.
- `conftest.py` — Confirm the repo-root conftest continues to arm the guard correctly from a worktree (helper-side fix preferred over conftest change).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — Document main-checkout anchoring and the two false-positive classes.
- `skill/shared/tests/` / `tests/` — New regression tests; `tests/fixtures/` or helper fixtures if a nested-worktree harness is needed.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the operator intends the anchor fix (AC1–AC3, AC5) as the core scope; the worktree-registration churn (AC4) is included because it is the same guard code path and the same symptom class. If the producer prefers, AC4 can be split into a follow-up work item — recorded here rather than silently dropped.
- **Risk (implementation):** relying on `git worktree list --porcelain` ordering (main worktree first) is documented git behaviour but somewhat implicit; prefer `--git-common-dir` or validate the first entry to avoid a fragile assumption.
- **Risk (regression / security):** an incorrect anchor could over- or under-exclude and either mask the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX incident or keep the false positive. Mitigated by AC3 (no false negative) and the existing contract tests.
- **Risk (scope creep):** expanding into a general refactor of the guard. Recorded mitigation: keep changes surgical to the anchoring + fingerprint decision and link any extra opportunity as a separate work item.
- **Risk (performance):** the extra main-root resolution must be cached per snapshot so the per-test fingerprint stays cheap.
- **Risk (test flakiness):** the nested-pytest tests must remain hermetic under `tmp_path` (use the existing `git_sandbox` factories, never the live checkout).

## Related work

- `SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ` — repo-root conftest live-repo guard (introduced the inner guard).
- `SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H` — `run_tests.py` live-repo snapshot guard (the outer guard that shares the helper).
- `SA-0MUG30IIR00978CW` — hermetic git sandbox helper and migration (owns `git_sandbox.py`).
- `SA-0MUG30HV8004HV94` — guard contract tests and guard-fires proof.
- `SA-0MUG30KEV006RBAM` — document hermetic-git requirement and guard.
- `SA-0MUH5KFDV002ORSS` — live-repo guard teardown ordering (adjacent `live_repo_guard.py` defect; shows the same test file is the home for guard regressions).
- `SA-0MUH1MJL6003767Q` — `implement.py run_tests` bypasses `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` (adjacent guard-activation defect; not blocking, but touching the same guard read-path).
- `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` — leaked `GIT_DIR` incident (the guard's reason to exist; must stay detected).
- `SA-0MU89WA740004GOJ` — destructive `init` commit wiped repo on `dev` (test-isolation incident context).
- `SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF` — multi-agent audit/test coordination (the contention context that makes this reproducible).
- `SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` — audit-runner pre-review bypass (source item; `discovered-from`).
- `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` — remote `dev` corruption / test isolation (origin of `git_sandbox.py` and the snapshot design).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — incident write-up and guarded-worktree proof; documents the snapshot/exclusion contract.
- `docs/dev/repro_live_repo_leak.py` — reproduction harness for the leak class the guard protects.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`) already contained the problem, root-cause pointer, expected behaviour, measurable ACs, and related work, and the defect was reproduced directly during intake. Questions below were resolved by repo investigation and recorded for auditability.

- Q: "Is `excluded_refs` really empty when the guard runs inside a linked worktree?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` returned `excluded_refs == set()`, while the same call from the main checkout returned 12 agent-worktree refs. Evidence: `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` (`agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`) and the 2026-09-26 reproduction on `dev @ 10995367`.
- Q: "Does `run_tests.py`'s outer guard share the same defect?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` and `diff_snapshots`, both from the shared helper; the conftest guard does the same. Evidence: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `conftest.py`.
- Q: "Is there an adjacent false positive from concurrent worktree registration/deregistration?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): Yes. `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))` and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails on any fingerprint change, so registering a second worktree mid-run fails the guard even though `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False`. Reproduced with a temp repo: adding `wl-two` changed the fingerprint while the diff stayed clean. Assumed in scope (AC4) as the same guard path; flagged for producer confirmation.
- Q: "Should the fix change the root the conftest/`run_tests.py` pass in, or the helper?" — Answer (agent, decision): the **helper** (`git_sandbox.py`) so both guards benefit and cannot drift (AC5). The passed root may legitimately be a worktree; the helper must resolve the main checkout itself.

```
live-repo mutation detected during skill/shared/tests/test_queue.py::test_remove_takes_specific_item_only:

```

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

The failure is a **false positive in the live-repo mutation guard**, not a defect in `test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` (the test passes in isolation on `dev @ edfbdfcd`). The `"(no differences)"` text is the tell-tale: the guard decided the checkout had mutated but could not render a single reportable change.

`skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py::pytest_runtest_teardown` fails a test when the **cheap fingerprint** changes:

- `LiveRepoMutationGuard` stores `self._baseline = fingerprint(snapshot_repo_state(root, include_status=False))` at session start.
- On teardown it compares `fingerprint(...)` again and `pytest.fail`s when they differ, rendering the failure with `describe_diff(diff_snapshots(self.before, current))`.

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::fingerprint` returns `(refs-minus-excluded, config, sorted(excluded_refs))`, but `diff_snapshots` **filters `excluded_refs` out of both sides** and never puts them in a diff category. Therefore a change **only in the `excluded_refs` set** changes the fingerprint (guard fails) while `describe_diff` has nothing to print → `"(no differences)"`.

`excluded_refs` is derived from `git worktree list --porcelain` for branches checked out under `<checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/`. On this shared multi-agent host, `implement.py start`/`finish` register and remove agent worktrees continuously, so the excluded set churns mid-run and trips the per-test guard against whichever test happens to be running — `test_remove_takes_specific_item_only` here.

Reproduced deterministically against the two helpers (same inputs, one worktree registration):

```
fingerprint differs: True
diff changed: False
describe:   (no differences)
```

Related triage-bot evidence on this item shows the same class of churn with a non-empty diff (`deleted ref refs/heads/wl-SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ-...` + `deleted config branch.wl-...`), confirming concurrent agent-worktree registration/removal is the trigger.

Fixing this item separately would edit the same helper concurrently and produce conflicting changes.
- **Related:** SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH — *Live-repo guard: shared refs/stash causes spurious mutation failures across concurrent worktrees* (shared-ref churn; different surface, same "spurious guard failure" family).

## Summary

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py::plan-approval-gate` fails to request producer approval for items whose effort is a t-shirt size (XS/S/M/L/XL) or whose risk is `Severe`. The skill contract states "Absent effort/risk → default conservatively to requesting approval (a human checkpoint is never silently skipped)" and the gate should request approval when effort is Medium/Large/Extra Large OR risk is High or higher — but the vocabulary sets do not match the values `wl` actually stores.

Discovered during planning of **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** (effort `M`, risk `Severe`): the gate returned `request_approval: false`, so a Severe-risk security/data-loss item would have silently skipped the human checkpoint. The plan session escalated manually instead.

**discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX**

## Evidence

- `wl show SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --json` → `"effort": "M"`, `"risk": "Severe"`.
- `python3 skill/plan/plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` → `{"request_approval": false, ...}` before this work item was raised.
- `PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT` contains full words (`Medium`, `Large`, `Extra Large`); `PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK` contains only `High`.

## Proposed fix

- Normalise effort (accept both `M`/`Medium` etc.) and include `Severe` in the risk set, or compare against the canonical `wl` value vocabulary.
- Add unit tests covering every effort/risk combination, including the absent-value conservative default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` for effort `M`/`L`/`XL` and for risk `High`/`Severe`, using the values `wl` stores.
- [ ] Both t-shirt abbreviations and full words are accepted for effort.
- [ ] Absent/unrecognised effort or risk still defaults conservatively to requesting approval.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the full effort × risk matrix, including the `M`/`Severe` case from SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX.

- skill/plan/plan_helpers.py
- skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py
